section.title: Overview
section.para: UAC AUTH (User Agent Client Authentication) module provides a common API for building authentication headers.
It also provides a common set of authentication credetials to be used by other modules.
Note that authentication provided by this module supports both qop "auth" and qop "auth-int" but if both values are presented by the server, "auth" will be prefered.

section.title: RFC 8760 Support (Strenghtened Authentication)
section.para: Starting with OpenSIPS 3.2, the auth, auth_db and uac_auth modules include support for two new digest authentication algorithms ("SHA-256" and "SHA-512-256"), according to the RFC 8760 specs.

section.title: External Libraries or Applications
section.para:
The following libraries or applications must be installed before running &osips; with this module loaded:
None

section.title: credential (string)
section.para: Contains a multiple definition of credentials used to perform authentication.
NOTE that the password can be provided as a plain text password or as a precalculated HA1 as a hexa (lower case) string (of 32 chars) prefixed with "0x" (so a total of 34 chars).

para.emphasis: This parameter is required if UAC authentication is used.

section.title: auth_realm_avp (string)
section.para: The definition of an AVP that might contain the realm to be used to perform authentication.

para.emphasis: If you define it, you also need to define auth_username_avp () and auth_password_avp ().

section.title: auth_username_avp (string)
section.para: The definition of an AVP that might contain the username to be used to perform authentication.

para.emphasis: If you define it, you also need to define auth_realm_avp () and auth_password_avp ().

section.title: auth_password_avp (string)
section.para: The definition of an AVP that might contain the password to be used to perform authentication. The password can be provided as a plain text password or as a precalculated HA1 as a hexa (lower case) string (of 32 chars) prefixed with "0x" (so a total of 34 chars) (for example "0xc17ba8157756f263d07e158504204629")

para.emphasis: If you define it, you also need to define auth_realm_avp () and auth_username_avp ().

section.title: enable_refresh_cnonce (integer)
section.para: Controls how the client nonce (cnonce) is generated when answering a digest challenge with qop. By default the cnonce is derived only from the server nonce, so as long as the server keeps re-issuing the same nonce, every authenticated request carries an identical digest response. Servers running a digest replay guard may then reject it (e.g. 403 Forbidden - Digest replay attack detected).

When enabled, the cnonce is seeded with the server nonce plus the Call-ID and CSeq of the challenged request, so each request gets a distinct cnonce and digest response. It applies to the modules using uac_auth that provide the Call-ID and CSeq: uac (uac_auth() function) and uac_registrant. The nonce-count (nc) is unchanged.
